subtopics.title: Standard Form and the Zero-Product Principle

questions.question: The zero-product principle says that if A × B = 0, then:
Why can you not solve (x − 2)(x + 5) = 8 by writing x − 2 = 8?
options: Because the brackets must first be swapped around
Because a product equal to a non-zero number can be split in infinitely many ways, so no bracket is forced to any value
Because x − 2 is smaller than x + 5

questions.question: Solving x² = 3x by dividing both sides by x is wrong because:
options: It loses the solution x = 0, and x might be zero — you may never divide by a variable
Division is not allowed in equations

subtopics.title: Substitution, and One Linear with One Quadratic

questions.question: In (x² − 3x)² − 2(x² − 3x) − 8 = 0, letting k = x² − 3x gives:
The full solution set of (x² − 3x)² − 2(x² − 3x) − 8 = 0 is:
For the pair x + y = 5 and x² + y² = 17, which equation should you rearrange first, and why?
options: The quadratic one, because it has more information
Either one — it makes no difference to the difficulty
The linear one, because it gives a clean expression with no squares in it
Neither; you should add the two equations

questions.question: The solutions of x + y = 5 and x² + y² = 17 are correctly written as:
options: x = 1 or 4, and y = 1 or 4, in any combination
x = 1 and y = 1, or x = 4 and y = 4

subtopics.title: Zero Is the Only Number That Talks

questions.question: In the stall analogy, two friends' earnings multiply to zero. You can conclude:
options: At least one of them sold nothing

questions.question: If their earnings multiply to R800 instead, you can conclude:
options: Nothing about either amount on its own — many splits give R800
One earned R800 and the other R1

questions.question: Dividing x² = 3x by x is compared to:
options: Removing a suspect from the line-up before anyone is questioned

questions.question: The correct treatment of x² = 3x is:
options: Divide by x, then add zero as a second answer
Take the square root of both sides
Write x = 3 and state that x ≠ 0
Write x² − 3x = 0, factorise to x(x − 3) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 3

options: Every term on both sides, including any plain number
Only the terms that are fractions

options: Only if the final answers look strange
Before the algebra begins, straight from the original denominators

questions.question: A solution that appears on the banned list must be:
options: Kept, since it came from correct factorising
Crossed out with a stated reason, which itself earns a mark

subtopics.title: Nicknames, and Keeping the Pairs Together

questions.question: Handing in the k values instead of the x values is compared to:
options: Giving someone a shopping list instead of the groceries
Removing a suspect from the line-up

questions.question: After finding k = 4 from the nickname, the next step is to solve:
Once you have x = 1 and x = 4, the partners y are found by substituting into:
options: The quadratic equation, since it is more accurate
The simple linear fact, because it is quicker and safer
Neither — the partners are simply the other x value

questions.question: Writing 'x = 1 or 4 and y = 1 or 4' as a final answer is wrong because:
options: The values are not in ascending order
It claims four combinations, and only two of them actually satisfy both equations
